entries.name: Mali Empire
entries.region: western Sahel and savanna, upper Niger (Mali, Senegal, Guinea)
entries.settlement: wealthy walled towns on the Niger (Djenne, Timbuktu, Gao): markets, mosques, Koranic schools, book trade
trade: gold from Bambuk and Bure (out, north)
entries.beliefs: Islam rising under Sundiata and Mansa Musa, over a deep Mande oral-tradition culture of hunters and smiths
entries.fell_by: succession crises; Songhai secession (1375); repeated Moroccan pressure until loss of Gao (1610)
entries.notes: The archetypal Sahelian gold empire: Mansa Musa's 1324 hajj depressed the price of gold in Cairo. Rich target for a caravan-trade loop in game.

entries.name: Songhai Empire
entries.region: middle Niger and western Sahel (Mali, Niger, northern Nigeria)
entries.settlement: walled caravan cities (Gao, Timbuktu, Djenne) with Sankore-style madrassas; floating market at Gao on the Niger
entries.beliefs: Islam (Askia dynasty, Qadiri-leaning scholars) layered on riverine spirit beliefs
entries.fell_by: Moroccan invasion with arquebus and cannon, Battle of Tondibi 1591
entries.notes: The last and largest Sudanic empire; Askia Muhammad built a university at Timbuktu. The fall of a gunpowder state to guns is the genre's best cautionary tale.

entries.name: Ghana Empire (Wagadu)
entries.region: western Sahel, southeast Mauritania and western Mali
entries.settlement: Koumbi Saleh: twin towns, one Muslim merchant town, one royal animist town, 5 days' camel from salt mines
entries.beliefs: Bida serpent sacrifice and Mande animism among rulers; Islam among merchant class
entries.fell_by: Sosso expansion and Almoravid pressure; eclipsed by Mali after Kirina 1235
entries.notes: The first Sudanic gold empire. Never confused with the modern country, though Ghana named itself after it in 1957.

entries.name: Kingdom of Benin
entries.settlement: planned walled city of Benin with radial earthwork walls (some estimates 15,000 km of ditches across the region), guild craft quarters inside the palace
entries.beliefs: royal ancestor cult; Oba as divine intermediary; later syncretized Christianity
entries.fell_by: British punitive expedition, February 1897, after the ambush of the Benin party; city razed and bronzes looted
entries.notes: The bronzes are the genre's best 'everything an empire can be proud of in one gallery' moment; the 1897 looting is a ready-made quest hook.

entries.name: Asante (Ashanti) Empire
entries.region: forest belt, modern Ghana and Ivory Coast
entries.settlement: Kumasi capital with concentric chiefdoms bound to the Golden Stool; matrilineal clans; great annual Odwira festival
entries.beliefs: Nyame the supreme god; ancestors; the Golden Stool (Sika Dwa Kofi) as the soul of the nation
entries.fell_by: British annexation after the wars of 1896 and 1900 (Yaa Asantewaa's siege of Kumasi)
entries.notes: Easily the most visually readable Akan state: stools, swords, goldweights, kente. Fantastic for a guild or regalia system.

entries.name: Great Zimbabwe (Shona state)
entries.settlement: walled capital of dry-stone enclosures (Great Enclosure, Hill Complex) with dhaka huts for commoners outside the walls
entries.beliefs: Mwari (High God); ancestor spirits (vadzimu); hill as sacred space
entries.fell_by: goldfield depletion, climate drying, shift of trade to Mutapa; capital abandoned by c. 1450
entries.notes: The largest precolonial stone construction in sub-Saharan Africa, built by Africans, no mortar. The soapstone birds are the country flag for a reason.

entries.name: Kingdom of Aksum (Axum)
entries.region: Ethiopian Highlands and Eritrean Red Sea coast
entries.settlement: imperial capital at Aksum with palaces, stelae fields, and harbor Adulis on the Red Sea
crafts: coinage (first sub-Saharan currency: gold, silver, bronze)
trade: ivory, gold, myrrh, tortoiseshell (out, to Rome/India)
entries.beliefs: pre-Aksumite gods (Astar, Beher) to Christianity c. 330 under Ezana, a bone-deep Ethiopian Orthodox tradition afterwards
entries.fell_by: loss of Red Sea trade to Muslims; soil exhaustion; capital moved to Lasta (Zagwe dynasty, c. 1137)
entries.notes: One of the four great powers of the 3rd century by Mani's account, and the first Christian kingdom in Africa. Ezana's stone is trilingual.

entries.name: Kingdom of Kush (Nubia)
entries.settlement: royal cataract-town capitals (Kerma, Napata, Meroe) with huge brick temples, palaces and tomb mounds; Meroe a great iron-working city
crafts: black-topped red Kerma pottery (hand-made, no wheel)
entries.beliefs: Amun-Re at Napata; Apedemak the lion warrior god at Meroe; Egyptian-style divine kingship, queens as kandake
entries.fell_by: Aksumite invasion under Ezana c. 350 CE; Red Sea trade diverted
entries.notes: The black pharaohs of Egypt's 25th Dynasty (744-656 BCE) and the most pyramids on Earth (at Meroe). Kerma to Meroe sits south of the desert belt; it is indispensable to any sub-Saharan catalog.

entries.name: Zulu Kingdom
entries.settlement: military homesteads (ikhanda) doubling as kraals and regiments; dispersed homesteads on hillcrests near water
entries.beliefs: Unkulunkulu (the Great One); ancestors invoked at ukubuyisa feasts; thunder-king Shaka as near-divine
entries.fell_by: British conquest after Ulundi 1879 (and the humiliation of Isandlwana earlier that year); annexation 1887
entries.notes: Shaka's military reforms turned a minor clan into a nation in a decade. The assegai and the ikhanda are instantly readable army tech.

entries.name: Ethiopian Empire (Zagwe and Solomonic)
entries.settlement: rock-hewn church capitals (Lalibela), later hilltop capitals (Gondar); monasteries and feudal kingdoms
entries.beliefs: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Christianity; Ark of the Covenant legend; Zagwe's Lalibela churches as new Jerusalem
entries.fell_by: 1974 Marxist Derg coup deposed Haile Selassie I
entries.notes: The only African state to repel European conquest decisively (Adwa 1896). Lalibela's churches were carved top-down from living rock, all eleven.

entries.name: Kingdom of Kongo
entries.settlement: Mbanza Kongo: palisaded hill capital with a stone cathedral (Sao Salvador); Mbundu and Bakongo provinces through elected manikongos
entries.beliefs: Bantu cosmology: world of the living and the dead separated by water; dikenga four-moment cosmogram; christianized c. 1491, deeply syncretic
entries.fell_by: Battle of Mbwila 1665, Kongo gone as a united power; final Portuguese annexation 1914
entries.notes: The first African state to voluntarily Christianize and correspond with Europe as an equal (Afonso's letters). The dikenga is a gift for a religious-UI mock-up.

entries.name: Oyo Empire
entries.region: Yoruba north and savanna (western Nigeria and Benin)
entries.settlement: walled Oyo-Ile (Katunga) capital of earthworks and palace quarters; garrison towns with cavalry barracks; massive metropolitan markets
crafts: Oyo leather work (much prized via Sahara)
entries.beliefs: Yoruba Orisa pantheon: Orunmila (Ifa divination), Sango (thunder), Ogun (iron); Alaafin as sacral king, ritually confined
entries.fell_by: Nupe and Fulani pressure; British annexation of the Yoruba hinterland 1896 (Alaafin's authority ended)
entries.notes: The cavalry nation of the savanna: Oyo's horse army gave it a reach no forest kingdom had. Sango is the genre's best thunder-god origin.

entries.name: Ife (Yoruba holy city)
entries.settlement: sacred city of the Yoruba, potsherd pavements, palace quarters, grove shrines; the spiritual mother of all Yoruba kingdoms
crafts: lost-wax (cire perdue) brass and copper heads
entries.beliefs: Yoruba cosmology: Oduduwa created Earth at Ile-Ife; Ifa divination system; Ooni as descendant of the gods
entries.fell_by: never conquered; eclipsed politically by Oyo and Benin, retained religious supremacy till today
entries.notes: Ife's bronzes were so naturalistic that early Europeans said 'the Greeks must have been here'. The best-kept secret of sub-Saharan art.

entries.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
entries.region: around Lake Chad (Chad, northeastern Nigeria, Niger, Cameroon)
entries.settlement: Njimi then Ngazargamu then Kukawa: camel-capital cities on the trans-Saharan nexus; Kanuri a dozen walled towns
entries.beliefs: Kanuri royal cult (Duguwa) to Islam from 1070s; mai as sacred king with fire-in-the-palace taboos
entries.fell_by: Rabih az-Zubayr's invasion 1893; absorbed into British Nigeria and French Chad
entries.notes: Twelve centuries of Sahelian statehood, one of the longest-lived empires anywhere. Idris Alooma (r. 1571-1603) rebuilt it with Turkish arquebusiers.

entries.name: Hausa city-states (Hausaland)
entries.region: Sudan savanna, northern Nigeria and southern Niger
entries.settlement: walled birni cities (Kano, Katsina, Daura, Gobir, Zaria, Rano, Biram) with Kurmi-style caravan markets and indigo pits
crafts: leather (Morocco-side 'morocco leather' is Hausa kuna kanta)
entries.beliefs: Bori possession cult and ancestral spirits, to Islam from 1349 (Kano); Bori persists beneath the surface
entries.fell_by: Fulani jihad of Usman dan Fodio 1804-1808; became emirates of the Sokoto Caliphate; British 1903
entries.notes: The urban commercial web that fed the whole savanna: leather for the Sahara, kola for the forest. If the game has a market district, it's a birni.

entries.name: Mutapa Empire (Mwenemutapa)
entries.settlement: Zimbabwe-state dry-stone political heartland, later dhaka palisades; Nyatsimba Mutota's diaspora capital near the Zambezi
entries.beliefs: Mwari (High God); ancestor spirits; royal lions as sacred regalia animals
entries.fell_by: Rozwi succession c. 1660; Portuguese coastal pressure; final partition in 1760 civil war
entries.notes: The direct heir of Great Zimbabwe, and the source of the 'Monomotapa' myth that sent Portuguese dreams of gold upriver.

entries.name: Swahili city-states (Kilwa, Mombasa, Zanzibar)
entries.region: East African coast and offshore islands (Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique)
entries.settlement: coral-rag stone towns with mosques, baths and wind-catchers; ports open to the Indian Ocean monsoon; stone towns with carved doors
crafts: coral rag architecture and carved doors
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam from ~8th century; Shiraz-descended sultanates; Swahili Shafi'i observance, distinct from Arabian Wahhabism
entries.fell_by: Portuguese conquest 1500-1700; Omani takeover 1698 (Zanzibar); British/German carve-up 1890
entries.notes: The coast's monsoon economy stitched Africa to Arabia, India and China for a thousand years. Ibn Battuta visited Kilwa c. 1331. The carved doors are iconic.

entries.name: Kingdom of Buganda
entries.settlement: kabaka's hilltop palace capital (Kasubi, Kampala) with bark-cloth-roofed temples; clan-based hamlets around hills
trade: ivory (out, to Indian Ocean coast via caravans)
entries.beliefs: Lubaale ancestral pantheon and Kabaka-divinity; syncretic Catholic/Protestant conversion from 1877; huge role of clan ancestors (ssaza)
entries.fell_by: British protectorate 1894; kingdom abolished by Milton Obote 1966; constitutional monarchy restored 1993
entries.notes: Bark cloth is the single most beautiful fabric on the continent: beaten, not woven. Kasubi tombs are UNESCO, and the clan system is a design doc for social simulation.

entries.name: Kingdom of Rwanda
entries.settlement: mwami's ibirule highland capitals with royal cattle enclosures; satrap provinces (ibinyarwanda) under ritual chiefs
entries.beliefs: Imana (supreme being); kubandwa cult of sacred beings; mwami as divine intermediary
entries.fell_by: 1959 revolution; monarchy abolished 1961; 1962 independence then 1990-94 genocide aftermath
entries.notes: Kigeli V was deposed by a Hutu-led coup in 1961, ending a sacral Tutsi monarchy. Be careful with this one; the design doc needs a note, not a romanticization.

entries.name: Kingdom of Dahomey
entries.region: Abomey plateau, modern Republic of Benin
entries.settlement: Abomey capital of six palace compounds with bas-relief appliqué walls; Ouidah port; garrison towns on the plateau
crafts: the Mino (female palace troops, 'Dahomey Amazons') drilling
entries.beliefs: Fon vodun (Dan the rainbow serpent); Vodun rites; ancestors; sanctuary rites for drowning
entries.fell_by: French conquest 1894 (Battle of Poguessa); King Béhanzin exiled to Martinique then Algeria
entries.notes: The only sub-Saharan state with a fully institutionalized female army (Mino). Ganvié, the stilt village built by Tofinu fleeing them, is still lived in.

entries.name: Igbo of Nri (Nri kingdom and Igbo-Ukwu)
entries.settlement: no kings: village assemblies and yam-feast democracies; Nri as sacred (not military) priest-kingdom; Igbo-Ukwu hoards reveal 9th-century ritual power
crafts: lost-wax and bronze-casting (Igbo-Ukwu, c. 900, the oldest in West Africa)
entries.beliefs: Chukwu (supreme), ala (earth, moral law), ikenga (personal shrine of achievement), Ani; no priesthood above the village
entries.fell_by: British Aro expedition 1901-02 (Aro Confederacy collapsed); Nri priests submitted 1911
entries.notes: The democracy of the lower Niger: no kings, no central army, and bronzes older than Ife's. A direct rebuke to 'state = civilization'.

entries.name: Maasai (Loita, Kisonko, etc)
entries.region: rift valley and savanna of Kenya and northern Tanzania
entries.settlement: manyatta bomas: thorn-fence kraals with dung-plastered huts (enkaji), moved seasonally; age-set moran camps out in the bush
entries.beliefs: Enkai (Enkai Ngai, supreme being split male/female); laibon prophet-diviners; cattle as sacred trust
entries.fell_by: never unified into a state; colonized piecemeal British (Kenya) and German (Tanzania); reserves carved from grazing land 1948-1960s
entries.notes: The genre's default 'noble pastoralist warrior', for better and worse. Their manyatta are literal walking settlements; great for nomad AI.

entries.name: Basotho (Moshoeshoe's Lesotho)
entries.settlement: mountain fortress villages (Thaba Bosiu was Moshoeshoe's mesa); stone-terraced sorghum fields; cattle kraals at the core
crafts: Basotho blankets (iconic: stripes + shield emblem, still worn)
trade: wool and mohair (out, huge, to Britain)
entries.beliefs: Modimo (supreme being); ancestors (balimo); thunder and rain-maker priests (baroka)
entries.fell_by: never conquered; British protectorate 1868 to escape Boer annexation; independent 1966 as Lesotho
entries.notes: The highland refuge: Moshoeshoe united disparate clans on an unconquerable mesa and never lost a war. The Basotho blanket is a ready-made item icon.

entries.name: San (Bushmen; //Xam, !Kung, Ju/'hoansi)
entries.region: Kalahari basin (Botswana, Namibia, South Africa, Angola)
entries.settlement: no fixed settlement: seasonal camps of grass huts (san_grass_hut), ostrich-egg caches, waterhole territories
entries.beliefs: n/um trance dance; Kaggen the mantis creator; //Xam Bleek-Lloyd archive is the only written record of a hunter-gatherer religion
entries.fell_by: displaced by Bantu expansion (c. 1500 BP) and settler frontier massacres; land loss; not a state, so slowly dispossessed rather than conquered
entries.notes: The oldest continuous culture on Earth, with a 40,000-year art record. The Drakensberg galleries and the /Xam archive are museum-grade content.

entries.name: Khoikhoi (Nama, !Ora, Griqua)
entries.region: Cape region and central highlands (South Africa, Namibia)
entries.settlement: pastoral clan camps with matjieshuis (reed mat domes) arranged in arcs around the kraal; moved seasonally to good grazing
trade: sheep and cattle (out, to Bantu groups and later Europeans)
entries.beliefs: Tsui-!goab (supreme 'wounded knee' being); Heitsi-eibib trickster-hero ancestor
entries.fell_by: smallpox epidemics 1713 on; settler dispossession; forced labor; Griqua migration north (Adam Kok)
entries.notes: The first people the Dutch met at the Cape (1652): cattle, mats, and the word 'Hottentot' as Europeans butchered 'Khoikhoi'. Autshumato and Krotoa are tragic founding figures.

entries.name: Kikuyu (Gikuyu and Mumbi)
entries.region: Kenya highlands, Mount Kenya and Aberdares
entries.settlement: small mbari (clan) hamlets of thatched round huts within thorn-fence homesteads; no centralized state; council of elders (kiama)
entries.beliefs: Ngai (supreme being) dwells at Mount Kenya (Kirinyaga); ancestors; elders as ritual authorities (irungu)
entries.fell_by: British East Africa Company / Uganda Railway 1890s; land alienation 'white highlands'; Mau Mau 1952-60; independence 1963
entries.notes: The highland farming people who became Kenya's largest ethnic group and absorbed colonial expropriation. Mount Kenya as a real god-dwelling is a gift for level design.

entries.name: Mapungubwe (Kingdom of Mapungubwe)
entries.settlement: class-stratified hill capital: elite on the rain-making hilltop, commoners in the valley below; first Zimbabwe-culture state
crafts: gold metalwork (Gold Rhino, found on the hill, c. 1220-1300)
trade: gold (out, to Indian Ocean via Sofala)
entries.beliefs: Zimbabwe-culture ancestor/high-god tradition (ancestral to Great Zimbabwe's Mwari)
entries.fell_by: climate drying and goldfield exhaustion; trade shifted north to Great Zimbabwe c. 1220; abandoned
entries.notes: Southern Africa's first state, hiding in a national park. The golden rhino is the single most spectacular precolonial artifact south of the Sahara.

entries.name: Lunda Empire
entries.region: upper Kasai and Shaba (DRC, Angola, Zambia)
entries.settlement: Mwata Yamvo's capital at Musumba, and daughter Kazembe states in Zambia and Angola; ring of autonomous provinces paying tribute
entries.beliefs: Chibinda Ilunga ancestor-hunter cult; divine kingship; divine kingship and the sacred royal fire cult
entries.fell_by: Chokwe invasions armed with guns 1880s; Portuguese west, Belgian northeast; partition 1887-1909
entries.notes: The spiderweb state: Kazembe in Zambia, Kasanje in Angola, all Lunda-connected. Mwata Yamvo's court controlled the transcontinental ivory flow.

entries.name: Luba Kingdom (Luba Empire)
entries.settlement: Kisale-basin royal centers with memory-board (lukasa) archives; tributary villages in the Upemba depression
crafts: lukasa memory boards (oral history census in beads and shells)
entries.beliefs: Divine kingship (mulopwe); kalala Ilunga myth; memory-keeper guild (mbudye) guards the royal charter
entries.fell_by: Chokwe invasion and Belgian conquest 1889-1910; last mwami died 1909
entries.notes: The inventors of the lukasa memory board, the closest thing Africa has to a written constitution that just happens to be a beaded sculpture.

entries.name: Kuba Kingdom
entries.settlement: federation capital at Nsheng (Mushenge) under the Nyimi king; autonomous Bushongo, Ngongo and Kete constituent states
entries.beliefs: Woot, the divine ancestor; Nyimi as sacred king; ntudila (ancestral spirits)
entries.fell_by: never conquered before colonialism; absorbed into Belgian Congo c. 1910; Nyimi still recognized today
entries.notes: The Kuba carved the first life-size royal portrait statues (ndop) in Central Africa, and their raffia velvets are technically embroidery. The single richest art source in the region.

entries.name: Kingdom of Ndongo (Mbundu)
entries.settlement: hill-fort towns (Pungo a Ndongo, Matamba); Portuguese-occupied Luanda as the slave-trade hub they could not dislodge
crafts: nzimbu-shell currency beadwork (imported from Luanda island)
entries.beliefs: Ngolo/local ancestral spirits; Portuguese pushed Catholicism; Nzinga was baptized but died a traditionalist
entries.fell_by: Portuguese expansion from Luanda 1619-71; Battle of Pungo a Ndongo and annexation; final control of Matamba 1744
entries.notes: Queen Nzinga: diplomat, general, and the reason the Portuguese spent 50 years not winning Angola. The origin of the word 'Angola'.

entries.name: Sokoto Caliphate (Fulani jihad)
entries.region: northwest and central Nigeria, southern Niger and Cameroon
entries.settlement: walled emirate city capitals (Sokoto, Gwandu, Kano, Zaria and its Nupe fringe); Fulani horsemen as jihad cavalry
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam (Qadiri order); Usman dan Fodio's revivalist jihad as a moral state
entries.fell_by: British conquest after Battle of Burmi 1903; Caliphate dissolved; Sultanate of Sokoto continues as religious authority
entries.notes: The largest indigenous Islamic empire in African history at its founding: a third of modern Nigeria. The caliphate stopped the cavalry age by replacing it.

entries.name: Adal Sultanate (Horn of Africa Muslim)
entries.settlement: walled Harar jugol and Zeila (Saylac) port; garrison of Turkish arquebusiers under Imam Ahmad 'Gran'
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam; Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's jihad against Christian Ethiopia 1529-43
entries.fell_by: Battle of Wayna Daga 1543, Ethiopian-Portuguese alliance; Harar emirate persisted until Menelik II 1887
entries.notes: The other side of the 16th-century Ethiopian story: Gran conquered most of Ethiopia in 14 years, then died at Wayna Daga. A completely plausible rival civilization for a strategy game.

entries.name: Nok culture
entries.settlement: no known towns; dispersed farming hamlets with smelting and sculpture sites (Taruga, Samun Dukiya)
crafts: terracotta figurines (the earliest known large sculptural tradition in sub-Saharan Africa)
iron smelting (c. 800-500 BCE, arguably independent invention)
trade: later influences on Ife and Benin terracotta and bronze traditions
entries.beliefs: unknown; figurines seem funerary and possibly ancestor-venerating
entries.fell_by: disappeared c. turn of the era; unknown why; iron tradition continued into later Nigerian cultures
entries.notes: The African Iron Age's opening act and the source-code of Nigerian sculpture. Nobody knows what they called themselves; a designer can invent it.

entries.name: Sao culture
entries.settlement: fortified mound-towns (tel) scattered across the drying lake bed; walls of fired brick and clay
entries.beliefs: unknown; ancestor-figures and horsemen suggest heroic-age elites
entries.fell_by: absorption into Kanem-Bornu and later Wadai; Sao as an ethnic group gone by 1500 CE
entries.notes: The ghost civilization of the drowned lake: at least 350 mounds surround Lake Chad, filled with bronzes and bricks. Kotoko villages still make their pots.

entries.name: Jenne-jeno (Inland Niger Delta urban cluster)
subsistence: fish (huge, delta: catfish, tilapia, Nile perch)
entries.settlement: specialized-craft-town cluster (Jenne-jeno, Hambarketolo, Kaniana) on delta levees; no kings; iron- and pottery-casts side by side
entries.beliefs: ancestor-cult with clay-figure deposits; no temples found; possibly caste-structured (smiths vs farmers)
entries.fell_by: rise of Islam and urban Djenne (c. 1200); absorbed by Mali Empire; twin ruins abandoned by c. 1400
entries.notes: Proof that cities can exist without kings: a 2,000-year-old Niger delta commercial republic. The predecessor of Djenne, the mosque's ancestor.

entries.name: Zagwe dynasty (Lalibela)
entries.settlement: Adeffa and Roha (later Lalibela) capitals; monocentric cave capitals carved from living tuff
entries.beliefs: Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity; Lalibela as the 'new Jerusalem' against Muslim pressure (Saladin had taken Jerusalem 1187)
entries.fell_by: Yekuno Amlak's rebellion 1270 restored the Solomonic line; Zagwe never returned
entries.notes: Eleven churches carved top-down from a single hillside over a generation, each named and cross-shaped. The most ambitious rock-cut project in Africa.
